requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under UN R10.

An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10, except that no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.

A vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions and for immunity to radiated disturbances, with no tests for conducted emissions or immunity to conducted disturbances required for vehicle type approval.
ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 4 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband type approval limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband electromagnetic radiation values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 5.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 using a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband type approval limit shall be 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limit.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6.

Where vehicle immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

Where vehicle immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the field strength shall be 10 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 8 volts/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

Where vehicle immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6, in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the current shall be 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band and a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6, during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband electromagnetic interference value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

For the stripline method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the TEM cell method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the ALSE method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the stripline method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the TEM cell method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the ALSE method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the reverberation chamber method of Annex 9, the ESA representative of its type shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the ESA representative of this type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA shall be tested with the starting profile according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the ESA for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For ESAs that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor, the ESA subjected to the starting profile at immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems with 10 pulses shall meet functional status B for immunity related functions, and for functions not related to immunity related functions functional status C (for ESA which shall be operational during engine start phases) or D (for other ESA).

The ESA subjected to test pulse 1 at -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses shall meet FPSC III for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA subjected to test pulse 2a at +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems with 500 pulses shall meet FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA subjected to test pulse 2b at +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems with 10 pulses shall meet FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA subjected to test pulse 3a at -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h shall meet FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

The ESA subjected to test pulse 3b at +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for a test duration of 1 h shall meet FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
Unless otherwise stated in Annex 4, the vehicle broadband emission test shall be performed according to CISPR 12.

For a vehicle with an electric propulsion motor or hybrid propulsion system where the CISPR 12 operating mode (i.e. 40 km/h) does not activate all traction motors or auxiliary battery charging engines, an alternative steady state operating mode shall be agreed between the Technical Service and the vehicle manufacturer for the broadband emission test.

The vehicle broadband emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

The vehicle broadband emissions shall comply with the quasi-peak detector limits given in paragraphs 6.2. and 7.2. of UN R10, with a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 applied if peak detectors are used.
During the narrowband electromagnetic emission test the vehicle's electronic systems shall all be in normal operating mode with the vehicle stationary.

The vehicle shall meet the narrowband electromagnetic emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an outdoor test site (OTS).

The vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when the vehicle is subjected to electromagnetic fields according to ISO 11451-2 in an ALSE, with front irradiation for vehicles not considered as "large vehicles" (rear irradiation as specified in paragraph 5.1.3.), at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.

Where the alternative test method in an outdoor test site is used, the vehicle electronic systems shall demonstrate immunity when tested according to ISO 11451-2 in an OTS, with front irradiation for vehicles not considered as "large vehicles" (rear irradiation as specified in paragraph 5.1.3.), at the levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test at a vehicle speed of 50 km/h (respectively 25 km/h for L1, L2 vehicles) ±20 per cent, the vehicle speed variation shall not be greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, in case of an automatic gearbox, there shall be no change of gear ratio inducing a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed.

In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, if the vehicle is equipped with a cruise control system, the cruise control system shall maintain the required constant vehicle speed without any deactivation.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test with the cluster operating in normal mode, there shall be no unexpected warning and no inconsistent variation of the odometer.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test with the brake pedal not depressed, there shall be no unexpected activation of the brake and no unexpected activation of the stop lights.
In the "50 km/h mode" vehicle immunity test, all other failure criteria listed for the basic vehicle conditions (as far as applicable) shall not occur.
In the "REESS charging mode" vehicle immunity test, the vehicle shall not set in motion.
In the "REESS charging mode" vehicle immunity test, there shall be no unexpected release of the parking brake.
In the "REESS charging mode" vehicle immunity test, there shall be no loss of the parking position for automatic transmission.
The vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges in vertical polarization.
The ESA under test for broadband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The broadband electromagnetic emission limits for ESAs shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

Where peak detectors are used for ESA broadband emission measurements, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied to the limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10., which are for quasi-peak detectors.
The ESA under test for narrowband electromagnetic emissions shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

The narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA shall meet the limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that these results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition during the immunity tests.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements when tested in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, frequency step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with AM (amplitude modulation) test signal modulation, with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) test signal modulation, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) test signal modulation, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.
The ESA stripline immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
The ESA reverberation chamber immunity test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
The ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
The ESA shall limit conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply.

The ESA shall be immune to test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except for ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).

Every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under UN R175 shall bear, affixed conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, an international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2.

Where the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under UN R175, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the circle symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1, which need not be repeated.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.

The ACPE performance requirements shall apply to a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be forward.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be rearwards.

The ACPE shall regard as an accelerator control misapplication an accelerator control application having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control, and reaching a maximum position of the accelerator control of at least 90 per cent with that velocity.
The ACPE shall control acceleration when the vehicle is accelerated from standstill.
If the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
The information to the driver that the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the accelerator control is applied, provided that the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion and the weather conditions do not affect the performance of the vehicle (e.g. no storm, not below 0°C); the tyres are in an appropriate state and properly inflated, the brakes if intended to be used are properly operational, there is no severe uneven load distribution, no trailer is coupled and the mass of the motor vehicle is between maximum mass and mass in running order, and the vehicle's powertrain management system is properly operational; the ambient illumination conditions are at least 1000 Lux with no extreme blinding of the sensors, the target vehicle is not extreme with regard to Radar Cross Section or shape/silhouette (e.g. below fifth percentile of RCS of all M1 vehicles), there are no significant weather conditions affecting the sensing capabilities (e.g. heavy rain, dense fog, snow, dirt) and no overhead obstructions close to the vehicle; and the situation is unambiguous, i.e. the obstacle is stationary, unobstructed and clearly separated from other objects in the driving direction, the lateral offset between the centreline of the obstacle and the centreline of the vehicle is not more than 0.2 m, the direction of travel is straight with no curve and the vehicle is not turning at an intersection and following its lane, and the obstacle is a vehicle of category M1 or a wall like structure with a width of at least 2.0 m and a height of at least 1.0 m.

When conditions deviate from those listed for the ACPE collision prevention or mitigation performance, the ACPE shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy, as demonstrated in accordance with Annex 3.

Where a collision is not prevented, for a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2. are met.

Where a collision is not prevented, for a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of that speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

For vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the speed reduction shall be of at least 15 per cent.

During any ACPE intervention, the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE, where the intervention may be ended only when the obstacle is no longer detected or the driver has interrupted the function.

The effectiveness of the ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
The ACPE shall show conformity with the safety aspects of electronic control systems by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
The ACPE shall inform the driver of its intervention in accordance with paragraph 5.4.2.
The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
The interruption of the ACPE intervention shall be started by any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation.
In the case of interruption of the ACPE by maintaining the accelerator control application, there shall be no rapid increase of acceleration.

The ACPE performance requirements shall be met when verified using the test procedure as described in section 6, for a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant), except when the new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g., the operation of a stop/start system.
When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation.

When the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE (for instance in situations such as carrying a bicycle rack or towing a trailer), the ACPE shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are not present anymore.

When the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE (for instance in situations such as carrying a bicycle rack or towing a trailer), a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of automatic deactivation unless a failure warning is given as per paragraph 5.3.3.
A failure warning as specified in paragraph 5.4.3 shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of this Regulation being met.
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check.

In the case of an electrically detectable failure, there shall not be a delay in illuminating the ACPE failure warning signal, except that, if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time a failure is detected, the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.

A failure warning shall also be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical failure condition of the ACPE (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
The ACPE optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the ACPE optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

Each ACPE optical warning signal, except warning signals shown in a common space, shall be activated either when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
The ACPE intervention warning shall be given by an optical signal, which may be the flashing of the failure warning signal.

In addition to the optical intervention warning signal, a haptic or acoustic signal shall be provided to the driver, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
The ACPE failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the ACPE by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.

Following a "power-ON" and any bulb check, the ACPE failure warning signal shall remain illuminated if any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.

The ACPE shall be provided with a means, chosen by the manufacturer, to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal, or alternatively with a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE.
Natural ambient illumination during the ACPE test must be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux.

Where, at the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, tests are conducted under deviating test conditions (suboptimal conditions, e.g. on a not dry surface or below the specified minimum ambient temperature), the ACPE system shall still meet the performance requirements.
The vehicle equipped with ACPE shall meet the test requirements when tested at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg).

The vehicle equipped with ACPE shall meet the test requirements when tested at any other mass up to the technically permissible maximum laden mass as defined by the manufacturer, if this is deemed justified by the technical service.

In the accelerator control misapplication test, the ACPE shall meet the requirements with a lateral offset between the centreline of the target and the centreline of the vehicle of between 0.0 m and 0.2 m.

In the accelerator control misapplication test, the ACPE shall meet the requirements both with and without an expected ACPE intervention, both in a forward and rearward direction, and at least with the vehicle situated 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) from the target position at the start of the test, as detailed in Table 1.
The System shall be designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
The System shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.

The documentation package for The System shall give access to the basic design of The System and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
The documentation package for The System shall explain the function(s) of The System and the safety concept, as laid down by the manufacturer.
The documentation for The System shall describe, for periodic technical inspections, how the current operational status of The System can be checked.

The documentation for The System shall include a description giving a simple explanation of all the control functions of The System and the methods employed to achieve the objectives, including a statement of the mechanism(s) by which control is exercised.
Any described function of The System that can be over-ridden shall be identified, and a further description of the changed rationale of the function's operation shall be provided.
The documentation for The System shall provide a list of all input and sensed variables and define the working range of these.
A list of all output variables which are controlled by "The System" shall be provided, with an indication in each case of whether the control is direct or via another vehicle system.
The range of control (paragraph 2.8.) exercised by "The System" on each controlled output variable shall be defined.
Limits defining the boundaries of functional operation (paragraph 2.9.) of "The System" shall be stated where appropriate to system performance.
A list shall be provided collating all the units of "The System" and mentioning the other vehicle systems which are needed to achieve the control function in question.
An outline schematic showing the units of "The System" in combination shall be provided with both the equipment distribution and the interconnections made clear.

The function of each unit of "The System" shall be outlined and the signals linking it with other units or with other vehicle systems shall be shown, by a labelled block diagram or other schematic, or by a description aided by such a diagram.

Interconnections within "The System" shall be shown by a circuit diagram for the electric transmission links, by a piping diagram for pneumatic or hydraulic transmission equipment and by a simplified diagrammatic layout for mechanical linkages.
The transmission links both to and from other systems of "The System" shall also be shown.
There shall be a clear correspondence between the transmission links of "The System" and the signals and/or operating data carried between units.

Priorities of signals and/or operating data on multiplexed data paths of "The System" shall be stated wherever priority may be an issue affecting performance or safety as far as this Regulation is concerned.

Each unit of "The System" shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.

Where functions of "The System" are combined within a single unit or within a single computer, but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.

The identification of each unit of "The System" shall define the hardware and software version, and where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned, this identification shall also be changed.
The Manufacturer shall provide a statement which affirms that the strategy chosen to achieve "The System" objectives will not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle.
In respect of software employed in "The System", the outline architecture shall be explained and the design methods and tools used shall be identified.
The manufacturer shall show evidence of the means by which they determined the realisation of the system logic during the design and development process.

"The System" shall have design provisions built in so as to generate safe operation under fault conditions, for example fall-back to operation using a partial system, change-over to a separate back-up system or removal of the high level function, and these shall be explained to the Technical Service.
In case of a failure of "The System", the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

When "The System" is not deactivated by the driver, e.g. by turning the ignition (run) switch to "off" or by switching off that particular function if a special switch is provided for that purpose, the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.
If the chosen provision selects a partial performance mode of operation under certain fault conditions, then these conditions shall be stated and the resulting limits of effectiveness defined.

If the chosen provision selects a second (back-up) means to realise the vehicle control system objective, the principles of the change-over mechanism, the logic and level of redundancy and any built in back-up checking features shall be explained and the resulting limits of back-up effectiveness defined.

If the chosen provision selects the removal of the Higher Level Function, all the corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

The documentation of "The System" shall be supported by an analysis which shows, in overall terms, how the system will behave on the occurrence of any individual hazard or fault which will have a bearing on vehicle control performance or safety.
The safety approach at the concept (vehicle) level shall include consideration of interactions with other vehicle systems and shall be based on a Hazard / Risk analysis appropriate to system safety.
The safety approach at the system level shall be based on a Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA), a Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) or any similar process appropriate to system safety.

The safety concept of "The System" shall be validated, for example using Hardware in the Loop (HIL) testing, vehicle on-road operational testing, or any means appropriate for validation, and the validation plans shall be suitable and completed.
The documentation shall itemize the parameters being monitored by "The System".

The documentation shall set out, for each fault condition of the type defined in paragraph 3.4.4. of Annex 3, the warning signal to be given to the driver and/or to service/technical inspection personnel.

The documentation shall describe the measures in place to ensure "The System" does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when the performance of "The System" is affected by environmental conditions e.g. climatic, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress, ice packing.

The verification results of the reaction of "The System" to simulated failures of individual units shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
The vehicle shall be tested for radiated broadband emissions in the configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" (if available on vehicle) as defined in the flowchart of Figure 1.

The vehicle narrowband electromagnetic emissions test, for the configuration other than "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", shall be performed according to CISPR 12 unless otherwise stated in Annex 5.
The broadband electromagnetic emissions test of ESAs shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
For ESA other than involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emissions test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic emissions test shall be performed according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 8.
The ESA narrowband electromagnetic emissions test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.
Vehicles in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be tested with the test method described in Annex 11.

For systems that implement force-based triggering of the ACPE, notwithstanding paragraph 5.1.2., an accelerator control force greater than the triggering threshold shall be considered as accelerator control misapplication, with the performance requirements applying to a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.

Where a vehicle is equipped with a long term deactivation means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the system shall provide information to the driver that the ACPE has been deactivated by either a constant optical warning signal, periodic information, or, if deactivation is only for one direction of operation, a constant optical warning when the corresponding driving direction is selected.

Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and the constant optical warning option is used, a constant optical warning signal shall inform the driver that the ACPE has been deactivated, for which the yellow warning signal specified in paragraph 5.4.3. may be used.
Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and the periodic information option is used, the driver shall be periodically informed that the ACPE has been deactivated.

Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and the periodic information option is used, the information that the ACPE has been deactivated shall be given for a minimum of 10 seconds or until driver confirmation.

Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and the periodic information option is used, the information that the ACPE has been deactivated shall be given at least either every 7 days or every 10 engine starts (or run cycles, as relevant), not counting when a new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g. the operation of a stop/start system.

Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and the periodic information option is used, the information that the ACPE has been deactivated shall be distinct from the failure warning signal specified in paragraph 5.4.3.

Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and deactivation is only for one direction of operation (forward or rearwards), as an alternative to the constant or periodic information, a constant optical warning shall be given when the corresponding driving direction is selected for the first time following each initiation of the powertrain.
Where a long term deactivation means is fitted and deactivation is only for one direction of operation, the constant optical warning shall remain at least until the driving direction is changed.

Where a long term deactivation means is fitted, the long-term deactivation process shall be designed in such a way that deactivation of the ACPE shall not be possible with less than two deliberate actions.

While an Automated Driving System is in control of the vehicle (e.g. ALKS), the ACPE may be suspended or its control strategies adapted without indication to the driver only as long as the risks associated with a pedal misapplication remain mitigated to the same degree as provided by ACPE.

The target used for the ACPE vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or alternatively a "soft target" representative of a passenger vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the sensor system of the ACPE under test according to either ISO 19206-1:2018 or ISO 19206-3:2021 at the choice of the manufacturer.
